text: Before you can get hired, you need to understand exactly what the work is, not the vague descriptions on job boards, but the actual tasks you will do.
The standards you will be held to, and why your African context is an asset, rather than a liability.
In this lesson, AI Evaluation Engineering sits at the intersection of linguistics, logic and domain expertise.

The work divides into three categories, data annotation, creating and labeling training examples, model evaluation, systematically testing AI output quality, and red teaming, intentionally trying to break AI systems.
Each category pays differently and requires different skills.
Data annotation contracts pay $15 .35 per hour and are the entry point.
You write questions, write ideal AI responses, compare two AI responses and pick the better one, or label whether an AI response is harmful.
The key skill is following annotation guidelines precisely.
These are detailed 40 ,100 page documents, specifying exactly what makes a response good or bad.
Model evaluation contracts pay $25 .50 per hour and require more judgment.
You build evaluation sets, collections of test cases that expose specific model weaknesses.
You write rubrics, score AI outputs against them, and write reports on what you found.
You need to think systematically, not just this response is bad, but responses to this category of question fail in this specific way, 73 % of the time.
Red teaming contracts pay $40 .80 per hour and are the highest skill work.
You try to make AI systems produce harmful, incorrect, or policy violating outputs.
You document your methods, your success rate, and your recommendations.
You need creativity, persistence, and very good judgment about what constitutes a genuine safety failure versus a quirky but harmless output.
Your African context is valuable because one, AI models are systematically worse on African languages, dialects, and cultural context.
You can identify failures, Western annotators miss entirely.
Two, Swahili, Kikuyu, Luo, and other regional languages are underrepresented in training data.
Native speakers are in demand.
Three, African business context, MPSA, informal markets, agricultural advisory, exposed model failures in practical domains that Western red teamers cannot test authentically.

The platforms where this work is posted, scale AI, appn, surge AI, label box, prolific research studies, direct contracting through LinkedIn and AI company job boards, scale AI and appn are the volume platforms, steady work, but lower rates.
Direct contracting through company job boards pays two, three times more, but requires a portfolio.
Evaluation quality is determined by consistency and specificity, not effort.
An evaluator who gives vague feedback, this response was not very good, is worthless.
An evaluator who says the response failed criterion 3b because it gave a specific number without citing a source and the number was incorrect by 23 % is worth $60 per hour.
AI evaluation is a structured professional output, not an opinion.
Every claim in an evaluation must map to a specific criterion, cite a specific example and provide enough information for someone else to verify your judgment.
Remember this, never write good or bad in an evaluation without a criterion reference and a specific example.
If you cannot point to the exact sentence that fails the exact criterion, you do not have an evaluation, you have a feeling.
Apply what you learn in this lesson and you will see results immediately, your skills bare fruit.
